correctness.rationale: The integral bipartite transportation-flow theorem reduces feasibility of all degree-t exponent margins to k independent inequalities r_i+c_i<=t. Pairs of their violations are impossible. Double Vandermonde count yields exact coefficient formula for all t, including zero; Segre transform gives the Hilbert series; saturation yields normality and Hochster Cohen--Macaulay; palindromicity of h* gives the complete Gorenstein classification. An independently enumerating script passed 139 finite checks, used only as corroboration.

originality.rationale: The literature comparisons identify rank-one Segre completion, graph normality, general Ehrhart methods and multiplicity/Gorenstein criteria as existing. None of the accessible primary full text or actual research-database results supplies the additive \(-kz\) correction to the entire Hilbert numerator for all partial-matching deletions. This is a best-knowledge originality assessment with explicit full-text access residual risks; it does not assert global uniqueness. A later nonbipartite graph family with a one-term h-polynomial deficit is explicitly distinguished: the general pattern of a subtraction term is not the novelty claim.
residual_risks: Full text of Gitler--Valencia (2005) not accessible: possible hidden full-Hilbert computation despite abstract focus on multiplicity and Gorenstein.
Later deficient-complete-bipartite edge-ring article full text not accessible, although its available ring definition points to a different Stanley--Reisner construction.
General graph Gröbner/Ehrhart algorithms could specialize to matching deletion, but no inspected published formula was found; this is not a proof of uniqueness.

value.rationale: A natural class of sparse coordinate projections of Segre varieties admits an exact full graded Hilbert-function formula, a simple linear h-polynomial deficit and a sharp exceptional Gorenstein boundary. The exact algebraic-completion invariant is more informative than degree alone and captures the structural significance of a missing matching rather than an arbitrary small computation.
